Modern progressivism draws from at least three great American traditions: the Populist farmers and workers who challenged concentrated economic power and demanded a say over the economy, the New Deal which made economic security a duty of government, and the Black freedom movement which expansively defined economic rights as a necessity for political equality itself.


Ro Khanna (@RoKhanna)

I shared with Democrats at the South Carolina Convention today that my progressivism is rooted and influenced by the Black freedom struggle in America.

It is rooted in the vision of W. E. B. Du Bois, who insisted that political democracy without economic democracy would be incomplete.

It is rooted in the organizing of A. Philip Randolph who built the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters and showed that labor rights and civil rights were one struggle.

It is rooted in Bayard Rustin, who organize

Well said. And add Rustin/King's Freedom budget so it is truly inclusive for 21st century America!


Mike Young (@micyoung75)

The "FDR coalition" argument Khanna is making is specific: economic populism plus foreign policy moral clarity can win in contested states where neither party's standard formula has been working.

I am proud of @grahamformaine for having the character to stand up against the war in Iran, against genocide, and against an unfair & lopsided economy. I am proud of him for having a vision for a new deal for our time. Excited to campaign with him June 5!

I'm honored to speak at @scdp's convention this weekend alongside @ClyburnSC06 about the need to take on this Supreme Court, and the vision to bring modern wealth creation and technological opportunity to the Black South.

South Carolina didn’t have a single Black American in the state house or Congress between 1892-1970. I was honored to speak with Rep. Jim Felder who won in 1970 and made history. Every American needs to listen to his story.
